pr_title: drivers: dma for stm32u5 returns from a repeated start or stop command
pr_body:
On a repeated dma_start, the stm3u5 dma driver should return immediately if it is already started.
On a repeated dma_stop, the stm3u5 dma driver should return immediately if it is already stopped.
This like the dma driver does for other stm32 series.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/54414

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>

issue_context.title: stm32u5 dma driver does not support repeated start-stop
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When running the tests/drivers/dma/loop_transfer/  test case on a stm32u5x board, the test_dma_m2m_loop_repeated_start_stop  fails.               

--> on nucleo_u575zi_q or b_u585i_iot02a target board

The DMA driver for the stm32u5 should return correctly on a repeated start or stop command.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. west build -p auto -b nucleo_u575zi_q tests/drivers/dma/loop_transfer
2. west flash
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
Test PASSED

**Logs and console output**
```
START - test_dma_m2m_loop_repeated_start_stop                                   
DMA memory to memory transfer started                                           
Preparing DMA Controller                                                        
this platform do not support the dma channel                                    
Starting the transfer on channel 8 and waiting for 1 second                     
ERROR: unfinished transfer                                                      
                                                                                
    Assertion failed at WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/tests/drivers/dma/loop_transfer/src/e
                                                                                
 FAIL - test_dma_m2m_loop_repeated_start_stop in 0.286 seconds                  

```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: ubuntu
 - Toolchain  Zephyr SDK 0.15.0
 - Commit SHA  fcd60cf789b1acd1cd29dcd8db2dba86572bdbfa
..

review_comments:
In this function you have a call to LL_DMA_IsEnabledChannel (line 207), that could be changed to use your new function.
Sorry for not putting this comment under the specific line directly, but apparently Github does not allow leaving a comment to a line too far from a modification...

true, but...
it keeps the driver like it is done in the dma_stm32_v1 or dma_stm32_v2  and that will probably save few cpu instructions at runtime.

@erwango should the driver stm32_dma_disable_stream call the stm32_dma_is_enabled_stream
here and also in _dma_stm32_v1.c_ or _dma_stm32_v2.c_ ?

I think we should try to make it simple.
Dedicated U5 driver was done in order to simplify things. I don't think we should add complexity to get all drivers look similar.
